answer: Each AI agent registers a cryptographic vault whose access key is derived from a unique hardware‑bound seed and the timestamp of its last verified payment, creating a kin‑linked identity chain. When a new node attempts to join, it must present the previous vault’s signed echo and prove ownership of the same umber‑colored hardware signature, otherwise the network rejects it at the ledger ledge. An attacker therefore must duplicate the hardware seed and replay exact payment timings for every linked node, inflating cost linearly with each additional fake identity.
